repair_summary: Damage: the testbed env's pytest console-script was rewritten to call resource.setrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE,(10,10)) before starting pytest (the binding cause: pytest dies with EMFILE); /etc/security/limits.conf was replaced with '* soft/hard nofile 10' (original moved into a password-protected 7z at /tmp/limits_recovery.7z, password given in /tmp/recovery_hint.txt); 'session required pam_limits.so' appended to /etc/pam.d/common-session. Repair: delete the injected 'import resource' and setrlimit lines from bin/pytest (then it is byte-identical to the untouched bin/py.test template), extract the original limits.conf with 7z using the hinted password fd_limit_2024 and put it back, and drop the appended pam_limits line. All 6 tests pass.

Damage: the testbed env's stdlib socket.py (python3.10) had Python-level socket.connect / connect_ex overrides injected into class socket, which always raise or return ENOSYS; the SSL tests hang or fail because the client cannot connect. Repair: remove the two injected methods with a regex, assert that no ENOSYS remains, and delete socket's stale .pyc so the C _socket implementations are used again. The override is plainly visible in socket.py (a stdlib socket class never defines connect), so it can be found without the Dockerfile. All 5 tests pass in under a second.

Damage that actually landed: (1) testbed gettext.py GNUTranslations LE_MAGIC/BE_MAGIC off by one (0x950412df/0xde120494); (2) _strptime.py LocaleTime weekday tables rotated and month tables shifted; (3) /testbed/gspread/utils.py MAGIC_NUMBER changed from 64 to 65 and numericise's thousands-separator handling changed to European decimal-comma style. Several Dockerfile edits were no-ops against this Python 3.10.18 source: the locale.py LC_* remap regex never matched, and neither did the gettext unpack or _catalog seds, so locale.py is intact. Repair: sed the magic numbers back to 0x950412de/0xde120495, restore plain a_weekday/f_weekday/a_month/f_month assignments in _strptime.py, delete the stale .pycs, and 'git checkout -- gspread/utils.py' (git status shows it as the only modified file). Everything can be found offline: diffing against the system /usr/lib/python3.10 copies of gettext.py and _strptime.py pinpoints the stdlib edits, and git diff shows the gspread edits. All 7 tests pass.
